items.title: Yemen's Houthis advance on Aden as government forces retreat to defend their capital
items.desc: Houthi forces in Yemen have advanced to within 60 kilometres of Aden, the seat of the country's internationally recognised government, military and government sources said Sunday. items.title: Iran’s Pezeshkian warns against wartime misinformation
items.desc: Iran’s Pezeshkian warns against wartime misinformation Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told ministers the government would keep backing the military “around the clock and with all its capacity”, the Fars news agency reports. Pezeshkian warned against “misinformation and creating a negative atmosphere against the government”. He added that “we are in a state of war and the enemy is trying with all its capacity to create problems in the country”. He told the cabinet that “propaganda, accusations, and distractions will not undermine the government’s resolve”.

items.title: Houthis say they fired missiles at Riyadh airport and financial district
items.desc: Houthis say they fired missiles at Riyadh airport and financial district The Houthis say they fired two ballistic missiles at targets in the Saudi capital, naming the financial district and King Khalid International Airport. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group launched six more ballistic missiles at Saudi troops in Yemen’s southern Lahj governorate, targeting Qa’wa camp and nearby positions. Saudi Arabia has yet to respond. Al Jazeera reports that two explosions rang out in the Yemeni city of Aden.

items.title: Houthis deny targeting Mecca or Medina in Saudi drone attacks

Writing on Telegram, Saree said the group directs its operations exclusively at oil installations and military bases in Saudi Arabia.
